about: Routing regression fixture. Every ticket is written the way a human actually
drops one on the board — no role hints, no board vocabulary. `expect` is the
role that must own it; `alsoAcceptable` are defensible second choices that
still get the sandbox right. Graded by scripts/routing-eval.ts, which spends
one real triage call per ticket and is therefore not part of `bun run check`.
Baseline before the 2026-07-29 description fix: 5/8, with all three
judgement-shaped tickets landing on write-capable implementers.

tickets.idea: the /orders endpoint returns 500 when the cart is empty, fix it and add a regression test
tickets.why: One coupled implementation unit: the fix and the test that proves it.

tickets.idea: the settings modal traps focus and the close button is unreachable by keyboard
tickets.why: Accessibility defect in existing UI code.

tickets.idea: our staging deploy takes 40 minutes, speed up the CI pipeline
how many users churned last quarter and what correlates with it
tickets.why: Measurement and correlation, not a code change.

tickets.idea: review MR !442 in the payments service before we merge it
tickets.why: Judgement on code the board did not write. Regressed to `backend` at 0.92 confidence before the fix, which also removed the read-only sandbox.

tickets.idea: compare Temporal vs Airflow for our job orchestration and recommend one
tickets.why: An unmade decision answered from sources. Regressed to `devops` before the fix because the subject matter is infrastructure.

tickets.idea: audit our session handling for security problems before the release
tickets.why: Audit of existing code; must not land on a write-capable role.
Too vague to route. Must park below the confidence bar instead of dispatching a guess.

tickets.idea: add SSO login with Okta: backend auth flow, the login screen, docs, and a security review
tickets.why: Four specialist deliverables. The security review belongs to `reviewer`; it went to `generalist` before the fix.
